header.userPrompt:
# Make the bank-statement review page load only the expenses it needs

## Problem

The review page (`/bank-statements/:stmtId`) fetches **all** of the user's
expenses via `getExpenses` to find link-or-create matches, then matches
client-side. In production that is ~1000 expenses and growing (500/month cap),
while the page only ever uses expenses that are **unlinked** and **dated within
the statement's period**. The linked-row display already comes from the
statement response (`findRowLinkedExpenses`), so this fetch is purely for
matching candidates — of which there are only dozens.

Narrow the fetch so the server returns just the candidates, and add the
uniqueness the matching relies on.

## 1. Optional filters on `getExpenses` (update, do not add a new endpoint)

`getExpenses` has ~9 callers; 8 want all expenses (charts, reports, expenses
list, refunds, receipts, link picker, auto-reconcile). So add **optional** query
params, defaulting to today's behaviour (no filter), leaving those callers
untouched:

- `from: Option[LocalDate]` — include expenses with `date >= from`
- `to: Option[LocalDate]` — include expenses with `date <= to`
- `unlinkedOnly: Boolean = false` — when true, only expenses **not linked by a
  bank-statement row**

The `Response` model is unchanged. Server query adds the given predicates:
`WHERE user_id = ? [AND date >= from] [AND date <= to] [AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1
FROM bank_statement_row r WHERE r.expense_id = expense.id)]`.

**Critical:** `unlinkedOnly` means "no **bank_statement_row** link" — it must
NOT exclude receipt-linked expenses. A ticket-captured expense (receipt linked,
no row yet) is exactly the dedup candidate we want to keep. So the `NOT EXISTS`
checks `bank_statement_row` only, never `receipt`.

## 2. Enforce one row / one receipt per expense (indexes)

An expense is referenced by `bank_statement_row.expense_id` and
`receipt.expense_id` (child → expense FKs, both nullable, `ON DELETE SET NULL`),
with **no uniqueness** today, so an expense can wrongly be linked by several rows
or several receipts — double-counting a reconciliation. The intended invariant
is **at most one row and at most one receipt per expense** (one of *each* is
fine — that is the dedup: a receipt and its matching bank row on the same
expense).

Add, in one new evolution, partial unique indexes (the columns are nullable):

```
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX bank_statement_row_expense_id_unique ON bank_statement_row (expense_id) WHERE expense_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX receipt_expense_id_unique           ON receipt           (expense_id) WHERE expense_id IS NOT NULL;
```

Existing production data is already clean (no expense has >1 row or >1 receipt),
so no de-duplication step is needed. These indexes also serve as the index the
`unlinkedOnly` `NOT EXISTS` wants.

## 3. Translate the new constraint at the repository boundary

The write paths that set `expense_id` on a row or receipt must catch the unique
violation and surface a domain error (not a 500), matched by the constraint
name, at the repository boundary — per `.orca/reviewers/persistence.md`. No
check-then-write. Paths: `LinkRowToExpenseAction` (via the repo setting
`bank_statement_row.expense_id`), `CreateExpenseFromRowAction` (links the row to
the new expense — cannot collide, but the repo should still translate), and the
receipt→expense link path (`ReceiptRepository.linkToExpense` /
`ConfirmReceiptAction`). Messages like "That expense is already linked to another
row" / "... another receipt".

## 4. Client: fetch the narrow window

On the review page, the expense fetch (initial load in the page loader and the
post-action refresh in the content) must request only candidates: compute the
window from the statement it already has — `periodStart - 3 days .. periodEnd`
(fall back to the min/max of the loaded row dates, minus 3 days, if a period is
absent) — and call `getExpenses` with that `from`/`to` and `unlinkedOnly = true`.
No server-side scan of the statement's rows; the client passes the interval it
already knows.

Matching itself (`ReconciliationMatcher.matchRow`, the bulk link-or-create
behaviour) is unchanged — it simply receives a small candidate list instead of
everything.

## Out of scope

- No change to matching rules, amount/date tolerances, or the link-or-create
  behaviour.
- No data migration / model restructure (links stay as child → expense FKs).
- Other `getExpenses` callers keep fetching all (unchanged).

## Acceptance

- `getExpenses` accepts optional `from`/`to`/`unlinkedOnly`, defaulting to the
  current full list; existing callers are unaffected; the review page fetches
  only unlinked expenses within `periodStart-3 .. periodEnd`.
- The two partial unique indexes exist; linking a row (or receipt) to an expense
  that already has one fails with a clear domain error, translated at the repo
  boundary; `server/test` green.
- The review page behaves exactly as before, just with a far smaller expense
  payload; `web/Test/compile` passes and web tests stay green.

resultJson.description:
The bank-statement review page (`/bank-statements/:stmtId`) currently downloads every expense the user has (about 1000, growing by up to 500 a month) only to find link-or-create candidates on the client. The only expenses it ever uses are those not yet linked by a bank_statement_row and dated in the statement's window. This epic adds optional `from` / `to` / `unlinkedOnly` filters to the existing `GET /expenses` endpoint. With no params it keeps returning the full list, so its other callers (charts, reports, expenses list, refunds, receipts, link picker, auto-reconcile, MCP) don't change. The review page's initial load and its refresh then request only the narrow candidate window. Matching rules (`ReconciliationMatcher`, bulk link-or-create) don't change; they just get a smaller list.

The epic also enforces the invariant the matching relies on: an expense is linked by at most one bank_statement_row and at most one receipt (one of each is fine, since that is the receipt/bank-row dedup). This is done with two partial unique indexes in a new evolution. Every repository write that sets `expense_id` on a row or a receipt translates the resulting unique violation into a domain error, matched by index name and returned at the repository boundary, rather than a 500. There is no check-then-write.

`unlinkedOnly` means "not referenced by any bank_statement_row". It must never exclude receipt-linked expenses, because a receipt-captured expense with no row yet is exactly the dedup candidate the page needs.

tasks.title: Add optional from/to/unlinkedOnly filters to getExpenses (shared endpoint, server, ApiClient)
tasks.description: Extend `ExpensesEndpoints.getAll` (lib/api/shared) with query inputs `from: Option[LocalDate]`, `to: Option[LocalDate]` and `unlinkedOnly: Boolean` (default false, e.g. `query[Boolean]("unlinkedOnly").default(false)`), placed before `userAuth`. Thread them through `ExpensesController.getAll` → `GetExpensesAction.apply(userId, from, to, unlinkedOnly)` → `ExpensesRepository.all(...)` → `ExpenseDAO.all(...)`. The query keeps `WHERE user_id = ?` and adds `AND date >= from` / `AND date <= to` only when given, plus, when `unlinkedOnly`, `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bank_statement_row r WHERE r.expense_id = expense.id)`. Never touch `receipt` here. Keep the ORDER BY. Use Anorm `SQL"..."` interpolation for the optional predicates (for example `($from::DATE IS NULL OR date >= $from::DATE)` or an equivalent bound-parameter form). Don't concatenate raw strings. `Response` stays the same. In `ApiClient`, keep the parameterless `def getExpenses` with the same behaviour, delegating with `(None, None, false)`. Add a separately named method such as `getExpensesFiltered(from: Option[LocalDate], to: Option[LocalDate], unlinkedOnly: Boolean)`. Don't overload `getExpenses`, because the many `client.getExpenses.onComplete` / `fetch = () => client.getExpenses` call sites must keep compiling without changes. Update `McpDispatcher` to call the action with explicit `(userId, None, None, false)`. Update the Mockito stub in `McpDispatcherSpec` to match the new arity. Don't put default params on the mocked action (see brief). Tests: in `ExpensesRepositorySpec` ("all" should …), cover the from/to bounds (inclusive), unlinkedOnly excluding a row-linked expense, unlinkedOnly *keeping* a receipt-linked expense, and no filters returning everything. In `ExpensesControllerSpec`, add a happy-path test of the filtered client call and confirm the existing tests still pass. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "testOnly *ExpensesRepositorySpec *ExpensesControllerSpec *McpDispatcherSpec"`.

tasks.title: Partial unique indexes on row/receipt expense_id, with violations translated at the repository boundary
tasks.description: Add `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/12.sql` (`-- !Ups` only, like 11.sql) containing `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX bank_statement_row_expense_id_unique ON bank_statement_row (expense_id) WHERE expense_id IS NOT NULL;` and `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX receipt_expense_id_unique ON receipt (expense_id) WHERE expense_id IS NOT NULL;`. Don't add a dedup step. Wrap every repository write that sets `expense_id` in `ConstraintViolations.translating(...)`: `BankStatementRepository.setRowExpenseId` (used by LinkRowToExpenseAction and CreateExpenseFromRowAction) and `setRowExpenseIdForUser` map `bank_statement_row_expense_id_unique` → "That expense is already linked to another row". `ReceiptRepository.linkToExpense` (used by LinkReceiptToExpenseAction, CreateExpenseFromRowAction and the Telegram upsert) maps `receipt_expense_id_unique` → "That expense is already linked to another receipt". `ReceiptRepository.confirm` (ConfirmReceiptAction; sets the receipt and optionally the row on a new expense) maps both. Put the `translating` call around the `database.withTransaction/withConnection` block, as `CategoriesRepository.create` does. Actions don't change (no pre-checks). Tests: in `BankStatementRepositorySpec`, linking a second row to an already row-linked expense fails with the row message. In `ReceiptRepositorySpec`, linking a second receipt to an already receipt-linked expense fails with the receipt message. Also check that one row plus one receipt on the same expense is allowed. Optionally add a controller test (`BankStatementsControllerSpec` linkRowToExpense) asserting the clear error rather than a 500. Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec *ReceiptRepositorySpec *BankStatementsControllerSpec *ReceiptsControllerSpec *DocumentsControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Review page fetches only unlinked candidate expenses in the statement window
tasks.description: Add a pure function to `BankStatementReviewLogic`, e.g. `candidateExpenseWindow(statement: GetBankStatement.Response): (LocalDate, LocalDate)`, returning `(min(periodStart, earliest row date) minus 3 days, max(periodEnd, latest row date))`. `periodStart`/`periodEnd` are non-optional on `GetBankStatement.Response`, so the spec's "fallback when the period is absent" becomes including the row dates, which keeps out-of-period rows matchable and the page behaving exactly as before. The 3 days must equal `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`, so reuse that constant. In `BankStatementReviewPage.fetch`, replace `client.getExpenses` with `client.getExpensesFiltered(Some(from), Some(to), unlinkedOnly = true)`. The expenses fetch is currently started in parallel with the statement; it now needs the statement first, so chain it after `statementF` and keep merchants/categories/rules in parallel. In `BankStatementRowActions`, give `refreshExpenses()` the same window (add a field such as `expenseWindow: (LocalDate, LocalDate)` populated by `BankStatementReviewContent` from `props.data.statement`) and call the filtered method. Leave every other `getExpenses` caller untouched, including `BankRowLinkPicker`, which needs all expenses. Tests: unit tests in `web/src/test/.../BankStatementReviewLogicSpec.scala` for the window (period-only, a row before periodStart, a row after periodEnd). Update any spec that constructs `BankStatementRowActions` or `ReviewData`. Verify with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec *BankStatementBulkRunsSpec"`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (see brief).

resultJson.brief:
LAYOUT
- lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/: Tapir endpoints (endpoints/ExpensesEndpoints.scala), models (models/expenses/GetExpenses.scala, models/bankstatements/GetBankStatement.scala), and ApiClient.scala, the sttp client used by both server controller tests and the web (`props.ctx.api.client`).
- server/src/main/scala/controllers/ExpensesController.scala: `getAll(userIdF)` → `getExpensesAction(userId)`; routes wire `ExpensesEndpoints.getAll.serverLogic(getAll)`. Server logic takes the endpoint input tuple flattened as params, so adding query inputs before `userAuth` turns `getAll` into `(from, to, unlinkedOnly, userIdF)`.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/GetExpensesAction.scala: `apply(userId)` loads expenses, merchants, splits, all receipts and all rows, then builds `GetExpenses.Response.Expense(... receiptIds, rowIds)`. Only the expense query needs filtering.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/mcp/McpDispatcher.scala:82 calls `getExpensesAction(userId)`. server/src/test/.../mcp/McpDispatcherSpec.scala:152 mocks it with `when(expensesAction(any[UUID]()))`. PITFALL: don't give `GetExpensesAction.apply` default parameters. On a Mockito mock the `apply$default$N` getters return null, which breaks stubbing. Call it with explicit args and update the stub's matchers.
- server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/: ExpensesRepository.all(userId) → daos/ExpenseDAO.all(userId) (Anorm `SQL"""..."""` interpolation, `${userId.toString}::UUID`, ORDER BY date DESC, time DESC NULLS LAST, created_at DESC).
- Link writes: BankStatementRepository.setRowExpenseId(stmtId,rowId,userId,expenseId,updatedAt) (withTransaction; DAO `BankStatementRowDAO.setExpenseId`, which updates only `WHERE expense_id IS NULL`, and 0 rows throws "Bank statement row not found or already linked to an expense") and setRowExpenseIdForUser (DAO `setExpenseIdForUser`). ReceiptRepository.linkToExpense(id,userId,expenseId) (DAO `ReceiptDAO.setExpenseId`) and ReceiptRepository.confirm(..., linkedRowId) (one transaction: ExpenseDAO.create, splits, ReceiptDAO.setExpenseId, optional BankStatementRowDAO.setExpenseIdForUser). Callers: LinkRowToExpenseAction:38, CreateExpenseFromRowAction:78/81, LinkReceiptToExpenseAction:26, ConfirmReceiptAction:72, telegram/UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction:60.
- Constraint translation helper: repositories/ConstraintViolations.scala, `translating[A](name -> message*)(block: => A): A`. It catches PSQLException, matches `ex.getMessage.contains(name)`, and rethrows `RuntimeException(message)`. Usage example: CategoriesRepository.create wraps `database.withTransaction {...}` inside `Future { ConstraintViolations.translating(...) { ... } }`. Reviewer rules: .orca/reviewers/persistence.md (scope by user_id, translate by index name, no check-then-write).
- Evolutions: server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/1..11.sql. The next file is 12.sql. Files use `-- !Ups` only (no Downs). The existing partial unique index style is in 3.sql: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON ... (...) WHERE ...;`.
- Web (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/):
  - components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala: `fetch(stmtId)` starts getBankStatement/getMerchants/getCategories/getImportRules/getExpenses in parallel and returns `ReviewData`; the content remounts on refresh (forceRefresh) and re-runs fetch.
  - BankStatementReviewContent.scala:68: `expenseList` state seeded from `props.data.expenses`. Line 112 builds `BankStatementRowActions(client, stmtId, setStatementRows, setSelectedRowIds, setExpenseList, setError, showToast)`. Line 215 passes `expenseList` to `BankStatementBulkRuns.handleBulkImport`, which looks up linked expense splits by id; the matched ids come from the candidate list, so a narrowed list still works.
  - BankStatementRowActions.scala:77: `refreshExpenses()` calls `client.getExpenses`; it runs after unlink and refreshRow.
  - BankStatementReviewLogic.scala: pure logic, including `ReviewData(statement, merchants, categories, rules, expenses)` and `expenseMatches(...)`. utils/ReconciliationMatcher.scala: `unlinkedByDate` filters `rowIds.isEmpty` and groups by date; `candidatesFor` looks back `0..MaxDateDifferenceDays` (3) days from row.date; `isMatchRowCandidate` requires `e.date <= row.date <= e.date+3`. That is why the window is periodStart-3 .. periodEnd.
  - `GetBankStatement.Response.periodStart/periodEnd` are non-optional `LocalDate`; rows have `date: LocalDate`.
  - Other getExpenses callers stay unchanged: RefundsPage, ExpensesPage, BankStatementAutoReconcilePage, BankRowLinkPicker, ReportsPage, ReceiptsPage (x2), ChartsPage. They use `client.getExpenses` without parens, so keep that method parameterless and add a separately named filtered method rather than an overload.
- Tapir: query params elsewhere use `.in(query[String]("filename"))`. Use `query[Option[LocalDate]]("from")`, `query[Option[LocalDate]]("to")`, `query[Boolean]("unlinkedOnly").default(false)`. ApiClient passes the input tuple to `handleRequest(ExpensesEndpoints.getAll, (from, to, unlinkedOnly, dummyUserId))`.

TESTING / CONVENTIONS (docs/guide/testing.md)
- Repo specs extend PostgresSpec, use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }` and RepositoryUtils factories (server/src/test/scala/utils/RepositoryUtils.scala: createUser, createExpense(userId, amount, date, ...), createReceipt(userId), createBankStatement, createStatement). Never seed with raw SQL. BankStatementRepositorySpec has a local `createRows(userId, descriptions)` helper and links with `repositories.bankStatements.setRowExpenseIdForUser(row.id, user.id, expenseId, Instant.now())`. Receipts link via `repositories.receipts.linkToExpense`.
- `should` subjects name the method/behaviour, never the class. Assert failures with `intercept[RuntimeException](...futureValue)` / `.expectError` in controller specs. Exceptions surface wrapped, so check `getCause.getMessage` (see ExpensesRepositorySpec:375).
- Controller specs (ExpensesControllerSpec, BankStatementsControllerSpec, ReceiptsControllerSpec) use the real DB plus ApiClient.
- Actions are not unit-tested. Web logic is tested as pure functions (BankStatementReviewLogicSpec); avoid new DOM tests.
- Every per-user query keeps `WHERE user_id = ?`. Don't use silent defaults or hacks.
- Verify with targeted runs only: `CI=true sbt Test/compile`, `sbt "testOnly *XSpec"`, `sbt "web/testOnly *XSpec"`. CI=true turns warnings into errors (unused imports/params fail). Don't run the full `sbt test`.
- Web tests need Node 24 on PATH; the default shell node is v16 and yarn install fails. Use NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider for web.
- BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec is known flaky under a parallel run; rerun before debugging.
- Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`.

id.name: Task: Add optional from/to/unlinkedOnly filters to getExpenses (shared endpoint, server, ApiClient)
Task: Partial unique indexes on row/receipt expense_id, with violations translated at the repository boundary
Task: Review page fetches only unlinked candidate expenses in the statement window

findings.title: Candidate expense window is frozen at mount and ignores edited row dates

reason.text: Took the 'document the limitation' option, because the scenario can't happen on this page. Nothing on the review page edits a row's date: confirmBankStatementRow is never called from the web, and refreshRow/unlink only change the link fields. A full refresh remounts the page and recomputes the window. Added a comment at BankStatementReviewContent.scala:115 explaining this. Passing live rows into the constructor would not have helped anyway, because onRowAction's useCallback keeps the rowActions from the first render.

findings.title: CreateExpenseFromRow can now fail halfway, leaving the expense created and the row linked

reason.text: False positive with respect to this change. receipt_expense_id_unique is keyed on receipt.expense_id, and CreateExpenseFromRow links the receipt to an expense it has just created, so no other receipt can already hold that expense_id and the new index can't be violated. The other failure mode, a receipt that is already linked, comes from ReceiptDAO.setExpenseId's existing 'Receipt already linked to an expense' guard, which predates this branch. Making the action transactional is a separate change outside this scope.
